sentences.text: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) rose from $96.6 billion in FY2016 to $182 billion in FY2025, a 7.3% CAGR [D5][D206].
Net income compounded at 9.7% and diluted EPS at 13.9% over the same window [F113][F115].
The path was a step change rather than a smooth compound: revenue grew 22.9% in FY2023 and 12.3% in FY2024 after a 5.8% gain in FY2022 [D179][D202][D154].
FY2023's jump came from higher net interest income on higher rates, with noninterest expense up 14% on compensation, the $2.9 billion FDIC special assessment and First Republic costs [P42][P36].
North America supplied the bulk of growth, contributing +20.6pp of the FY2023 revenue increase and +10.2pp in FY2024, at 77.9% and 78.5% of revenue [D245][D248][D243][D246].
In FY2025 North America grew only 0.3% (+0.2pp) while EMEA added +1.2pp and Asia-Pacific +1.2pp [D250][D251][D276][D301].
FY2025 net interest income rose 3% on higher Markets net interest income and Card revolving balances, largely offset by deposit margin compression and lower rates [P28].
Operating costs grew 1.4pp slower than revenue in FY2025, at 4.2% against 2.8% revenue growth [D225][D226].
Diluted EPS grew 1.4% in FY2025 against a 2.6% net income decline, as the diluted share count fell 3.4% [D216][D214][D224].
The efficiency ratio was 52.4% in FY2025 against a 57.2% window median, a 51.7% low in FY2024 and a 59.2% high in FY2022 [D207][D333][D331][D332].
The FY2025 efficiency ratio sat 9.3pp below the 61.7% banks peer median, the best of seven peers [D207][D337][D336].

Noninterest expense rose 4% on higher compensation, brokerage and distribution fees, auto lease depreciation and technology and marketing spend, partly offset by FDIC special assessment releases [P26].
Net margin of 31.2% sat 21.1pp below the 52.3% net interest income share of revenue in FY2025, with the 7.8% credit-loss provision and 21.4% tax rate the main drags [D210][D209][D208][D203].
Operating cash flow is not a meaningful earnings-quality measure for a bank; it was -$147.8 billion in FY2025 against $57.0 billion of net income [F60][F30].
The FY2025 outflow came from higher trading assets, higher securities borrowed, net loan held-for-sale originations and higher other assets, partly offset by net income [P21].
Capital return is the better test: buybacks plus dividends of $48.2 billion equaled 84.6% of FY2025 net income [D205][F30].
Return on average equity was 16.1% in FY2025, at the 100th percentile of seven banks peers against an 11.8% median [D213][D338][D339].
Loans were 57.3% of deposits in FY2025, up from 43.1% in FY2021, as deposits grew to $2.56 trillion and loans to $1.47 trillion [D211][D115][X207][X197].
FY2025 loans rose $121.1 billion, driven by CIB Markets and AWM securities-based lending on higher client demand [P4].
Buybacks of $31.6 billion and dividends of $16.6 billion in FY2025 helped cut the diluted share count 3.4% [X102][X112][D224].
Net income for FY2021 through FY2025 in the table comes from the proxy pay-versus-performance table, not the 10-K, and differs by up to 0.10% [R1][F26][X16][F30][X20].
The gap is immaterial to any trend here, but the 10-K figures should be cited where precision matters [R1].
FY2020 pretax income and income tax were later restated to $35.8 billion and $6.7 billion from $35.4 billion and $6.3 billion first reported [R2][R3][X63][X73].
The FY2020 recasts are small and do not change the pandemic-year margin conclusion [R2][R3].
The credit-loss provision rose to 7.8% of revenue in FY2025 from 6.0% in FY2024, at the 75th percentile of four peers against a 6.0% median [D208][D185][D340][D341].
Rising provisions alongside $48.5 billion of criticized exposure are the credit trend to watch, though the 1.8% allowance coverage is steady [P2][D212].
Whether the efficiency ratio holds below the 57.2% window median or drifts back toward the 59.2% FY2022 high, reported in the FY2026 10-K [D333][D332].
Whether the credit-loss provision stays above the 6.0% FY2024 level or falls back toward it, in the FY2026 10-K [D185].
Whether net interest income growth holds above the 3.1% FY2025 pace or turns negative as it did in FY2020 and FY2021, in the FY2026 10-K [D221][D100][D124].
